title: Cell Fusion and Gene Expression in the C. elegans Epidermis
text:
This project explores how cell fusion shapes gene expression and developmental progression using the C.
elegans epidermis as a model system. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing, CRISPR-engineered mutants, and
advanced microscopy will be used to uncover the molecular mechanisms governing syncytial cell function.
Insights from this research will improve understanding of normal development, diseases linked to defective cell
fusion, and the role of multinucleation in cancer and viral pathogenesis.

title: Targeting Pediatric Cancer Vulnerabilities
text:
Pediatric cancer, the number one cause of disease-related death in school age children, is still largely treated
with old approaches such as cytotoxic chemotherapy, radiation, and surgery. These childhood malignancies
typically express cancer-promoting proteins that make for challenging drug targets and generally have been less
responsive to immunotherapy approaches that have revolutionized the care of subsets of adults with cancer. We
will apply innovative, transformative approaches in functional genomics and chemical biology to overcome these
challenges toward new, paradigm-shifting therapies for children with cancer.

title: Mechanisms of sodium channel clustering at the neuromuscular junction
text:
Na+ channels are clustered at the neuromuscular junction (NMJ) and in a perijunctional
zone where they function to prevent synapse fatigue. However, the mechanisms
responsible for NMJ Na+ channel clustering and assembly of the perijunctional zone are
unknown. Here, we will determine the mechanisms responsible and investigate how
these change with aging and disease.

title: Dissecting the shared genetic mechanisms driving fentanyl addiction, cocaine addiction, and incentive sensitization using the Collaborative Cross mouse panel
text:
In 2022, fentanyl overdose was the leading cause of death for US adults aged 18 - 45. This striking statistic
underscores the urgent need to discover and characterize the genetic causes of fentanyl addiction, a highly
heritable disease. The successful completion of this project, in which we will use genetically diverse mice to
better understand the genes that cause individuals to abuse fentanyl, will contribute to the development of
novel, more effective addiction treatments.

title: Interneuron axonopathy underlies circuit dysfunction in a mouse model of Dravet syndrome
text:
Dravet syndrome is a severe neurodevelopmental disorder caused by mutations in the gene SCN1A and defined
by treatment-resistant epilepsy, features of autism spectrum disorder, and a high rate of sudden unexpected
death (SUDEP). The objective of this proposal, which uses innovative technical approaches in a well validated
preclinical experimental model system, is to establish impairment of action potential propagation along
GABAergic inhibitory interneuron axons as a key mechanism of Dravet syndrome pathology. The long-term goal
of this research program is to advance from clinical genetic diagnosis to inform mechanistically oriented, targeted
therapy in human patients suffering from what is currently an incurable and essentially untreatable disease.

title: Establishing the feasibility of measuring bereavement-related stress in a naturalistic setting
text:
The death of a spouse is a highly stressful life event that is associated with increased mortality and worsening
mental and physical health. Although bereavement is a dynamic process, limited data is available on the day-
to-day fluctuations in bereavement-related stress and the affective and physiological changes that follow. This
study will use ecological momentary assessment and continuous electrocardiography to measure affective and
autonomic stress reactivity among bereaved spouses in a naturalistic setting and has the potential of improving
our overall understanding of bereavement-related stress and its link to worsening health.

title: Harnessing human gut-derived Bacteroides to drive systemic anti-tumor immunity
text:
This research will further our understanding of certain common bacteria which reside within our intestines
throughout our lifetime, and how some of these bugs in particular can make our immune system more
aggressive. By researching the way these bacteria “communicate” to our immune system, it may be feasible to
pick the correct ones to package together as a probiotic. Such a medication could help cancer patients who
want their immune system to behave aggressively against their growing tumor.

title: Capturing, quantifying, and understanding combinatorial effects in small molecule signaling
text:
Chemical landscapes in biology are composed of thousands to millions of different small molecules, which
means that a cell or organism is always exposed to many different small molecules at the same time. The
overall goal of this project is to understand how biological outcomes may be driven by combinatorial effects of
multiple small molecules, with an initial focus on such effects in the context of host-microbiome communication.
This work may allow us to predict and manipulate effects of the microbiome on the human host and more
broadly will establish general models to describe signaling in complex chemical landscapes, which are
ubiquitous in biology.

title: The Role of Myeloid Cells in Parkinson's Disease
text: Parkinson’s disease is a brain disorder that leads to progressive movement and cognitive problems, and growing evidence suggests that innate immune cells in both the brain and blood play a key role in disease progression. This project will use a longitudinal study design, advanced molecular analyses, and patient-derived models to understand how genetic risk affects these innate immune cells over time, with the goal of identifying early changes and potential targets for new therapies.

title: Functional Genomics Core
text: The Functional Genomics Core (FGC) provides state-of-the-art experiment planning, sample preparation, quality assessment, library construction, DNA sequencing, and data analysis services to DRC members using state-of-the-art Illumina Sequencers including the high-throughput but flexible NovaSEQ 6000 system. We have experience with ChIP-seq, nucleosome mapping, whole exome and whole genome resequencing in mouse, human, zebrafish, and other species. We offer RNAseq, microRNAseq, GroSeq, CLIP-seq, nucleosome mapping, ATAC-Seq, ChIPseq, whole genome and targeted DNA methylome analysis, hydroxymethyl DIP, single cell ATACseq, single cell RNAseq and multiomics approaches. A goal of the FGC is to quickly adapt and occasionally develop new protocols for sequencing-based functional genomics analysis relevant to DRC members. We also offer a self-service sequencing services for advanced users at a minimal fee. Importantly, in response to DRC member requests, we provide extensive bioinformatics services, tailored to individual projects, to DRC members. The Core remains in high demand, with 46 current users. The FGC has provided data and analysis for over 70 research publications of DRC members during the past funding period and supported multiple grant applications. title: Project 1: Hypoxia and metabolic dysregulation as a targetable barrier to immunotherapy in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC)
text:
PROJECT NARRATIVE − PROJECT 1
 Despite the promise of immune checkpoint inhibition in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC),
only a minority of patients ultimately benefit. Continuing Project 1 has already identified tumor metabolism and
hypoxia as potential drivers of anti-PD-1 resistance in this disease and now seek to examine the interaction
between tumor hypoxia and metabolism, combinatorial immunotherapy, and response. The goal of this project
will be to identify the next generation of metabolically driven immunotherapy combination for clinical trial.

title: Targeting Undruggable Lung Vascular Enhancers with Compact AAV-Cas12f CRISPR Activation
text:
This project will develop a compact, single-vector AAV CRISPRa system based on the miniature Cas12f
nuclease to therapeutically activate distal FOXF1 enhancers in a neonatal mouse model of alveolar
capillary dysplasia. By restoring Foxf1 expression from the remaining healthy allele, this approach could
pave the way for treating fatal neonatal and pediatric vascular diseases.

title: The role of apolipoprotein E in Alzheimer's adaptive immunity
text:
Variants of the Apolipoprotein E (APOE) gene are associated with risk of developing Alzheimer's disease (AD).
This project will explore the role of APOE variants in the adaptive immune response to pathogenic viruses in AD.
The study will utilize genomic, proteomic and immunohistochemical approaches to interpret APOE-associated
adaptive immune changes to viral antigens in AD.

title: Training and Research on Severe Malarial Anemia
text:
This project supports advanced research training focused on severe malaria, severe malarial anemia, and related infectious diseases through collaborative activities in Kenya and the United States. The foreign component provides access to endemic disease settings, severe malaria cases, and longitudinal pediatric cohorts that are essential for training and discovery but are not available in the United States. In addition to malaria, trainees gain experience investigating important co-infections and comorbid conditions that commonly occur in children residing in western Kenya, including HIV-1, tuberculosis, and invasive bacterial infections. These pathogens contribute substantially to disease burden, immune dysregulation, morbidity, and mortality and represent major global public health challenges.

Because most Americans who acquire malaria abroad lack naturally acquired antimalarial immunity, studies conducted in Kenyan pediatric populations provide a uniquely relevant model for understanding severe malaria pathogenesis in immunologically susceptible hosts. The resulting advances in malaria, HIV-1, tuberculosis, bacteremia, pathogen genomics, surveillance, diagnostics, therapeutics, and disease modeling directly benefit American health by improving prevention, diagnosis, and clinical management of infectious diseases affecting U.S. travelers, military personnel, immigrants, refugees, and other at-risk populations. The program also strengthens U.S. preparedness for emerging and re-emerging infectious disease threats through advanced training in genomics, bioinformatics, epidemiology, and translational biomedical research.

title: Endothelial cell targeting of factor VIII for hemophilia A
text:
Gene therapy for hemophilia A aims to provide long term expression of clotting factor VIII to correct the bleeding
disorder. While the natural site of factor VIII synthesis is the liver sinusoidal endothelial cell, current adeno-
associated viral vector delivery approaches target expression to hepatocytes. The goal of this study is to use a
genome editing or a gene addition approach to target liver sinusoidal endothelial cells to achieve therapeutic
levels of factor VIII and to understand how hepatocyte and endothelial cell specific expression may impact
outcomes in gene therapy.

title: Molecular mechanisms of alkane hydroxylase (AlkB) reactivity and selectivity
text:
AlkB represents a large family of membrane proteins, the class-III diiron proteins, that help synthesize
critical fatty acids, lipids, and alcohols from bacteria to humans. This protein family includes
therapeutic targets for treating obesity, diabetes, attention deficit disorders, cancer, and fatty acid
hydroxylase-associated neurodegeneration. Understanding how these proteins work will contribute
fundamental knowledge of their catalytic reactions, generate insights for developing future
therapeutics, and inform new strategies for producing life-saving molecules.

title: Anticipation and integration in the primate visual system
text:
Vision science seeks to understand how the visual system functions and aims to develop treatments for visual
pathologies. The proposed studies to investigate how the objective of temporal prediction shapes the processing
of visual information in cortex will provide rigorous steps towards those goals. The obtained knowledge may help
to advance the treatment of cortical-based visual pathologies such as agnosia, dyslexia, and amblyopia.

title: Commercializing iDEP, an interactive and reproducible tool for analyzing RNA-Seq data
text:
RNA sequencing is a widely used technique for surveying the activities of tens of thousands of genes in
healthy or diseased tissues. Based on previous work, we will transform a web application into a
commercial product to help researchers with visualization, statistical analysis, and biological
interpretation of such data.

title: Mentoring the next generation of patient-oriented translational virologists
text:
The primary goal of this project will be to provide mentorship to trainees and early career investigators in
clinical studies and cutting-edge translational virology techniques in key priority areas of HIV research.
Trainees will help lead research to 1) Determine the virologic features of HIV persistence, 2) reservoir
mediators of post-treatment HIV control, and 3) Assess the impact of emerging HIV resistance to new
antiretroviral agents. The results of the studies will also advance our understanding of the mechanisms of HIV
persistence, post-treatment control, and the clinical impact of antiviral drug resistance.

title: Genetic Determinants of Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome
text:
Cardiac, kidney, and metabolic conditions, including cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, and type
2 diabetes, are leading causes of morbidity and mortality in the United States and affect individuals from all
backgrounds. These interconnected conditions, recently recognized as cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM)
syndrome, share pathophysiology and risk factors, including dysfunctional adiposity, dysglycemia,
dyslipidemia, ectopic lipid deposition, and hypertension. This project will investigate biological, genetic, and
other factors that contribute CKM syndrome.
